transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve started doing some things that don’t really make sense, especially at work and school. Like I’ll line receipts across the floor, or tap the calculator in sets of nine. Sometimes I just stand by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I’m okay. I know it probably looks strange, and I’m not really sure why I’m doing it.
When you do these things, does it feel like you have to do them to relieve an upsetting thought or feeling?

Not really like that, no. It’s not like I’m doing it to make a bad thought go away. I just kind of end up doing these things, like lining the receipts up or tapping the calculator in that pattern, and it doesn’t really make sense to me afterward.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is there?

Yeah… sometimes. If I’m alone at my desk, or walking home from class, I’ll hear a man’s voice say something like, “check line seven,” or “you missed the sign.” It sounds clear enough that I turn and look around, but there’s nobody there.
Before these recent problems started, did you usually have a hard time understanding other people or making friends?
I don’t think so. I mean, I was never super outgoing, but I could understand people well enough and I had a few friends. It wasn’t really a big problem before this.
Since these problems started, have you been having a harder time keeping up with your work or school than you used to?

Yeah. I used to handle my schoolwork and the bookkeeping stuff pretty routinely, but lately I’m not keeping up. I failed an important course module, and at work my ledgers have been coming back with serious mistakes. I’ve had to ask for help with things I used to be able to finish on my own.
Have people told you that your facial expression or voice has become much less expressive lately?

Yeah, a couple people have said I seem kind of blank or quiet. I still care about them, but most days I just… don’t really react much. I leave texts unanswered, skip hanging out after class, and even when they talk about music shows or art projects I used to be into, I feel pretty flat.
Have people told you that your speech has become hard to follow or jumbled?

Yeah, people have said that. Like at work, if I’m trying to explain why a ledger is off, I’ll start with the numbers, then suddenly I’m talking about tuition deadlines or tax rules, or even something like studio lighting and patterns in the numbers. In my head it sort of connects, but other people tell me they can’t follow how I got from one point to the next.
When you stand still with your hands held up, does it feel like your body gets stuck in that position and is hard to move?

Yeah, sometimes. Like I’ll be standing by the copier with my hands kind of held up, and I just stay there longer than makes sense until someone asks if I’m okay. It’s not always like I physically can’t move, but I feel kind of stuck and I don’t snap out of it right away.
Has anyone told you that you resist being moved, or that you stay in an unusual posture for a long time even after someone tries to change it?

I don’t know if I’ve resisted someone moving me, exactly. But yeah, I’ve stayed in weird positions too long, like standing by the copier with my hands up until someone asks if I’m okay. And I’ve been doing other stuff that doesn’t really make sense, like lining receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in sets of nine.
When someone tries to move your arms or body while you’re stuck in one of those positions, do you stay that way or resist being moved?

I’m not really sure if I resist being moved. I don’t think anyone’s really tried to move my arms much. What I notice is I’ll just stay there too long, like by the copier with my hands up, until someone says something. And I’ve been doing other odd stuff too, like lining receipts on the floor or tapping the calculator in sets of nine.
Has anyone ever placed your arm or body into a position and found that you stayed that way after they let go?

I don’t think anyone has actually put my arm in a position like that and checked. What’s been happening is more like I end up doing odd things on my own, like standing by the copier with my hands up too long until someone asks if I’m okay, or lining receipts on the floor, or tapping the calculator in sets of nine.
Has anyone been able to place one of your arms into a position and found that it stayed there after they let go?
No, not that I know of. I don’t think anyone’s tried placing my arm like that and then letting go to see if it stayed.
When someone moves your arm into a position, does it tend to stay there after they let go?

I don’t think so, not that I’ve noticed. It’s more that I’ll get stuck doing things that don’t really make sense, like standing by the copier with my hands up until someone asks if I’m okay, or lining receipts across the floor.
When someone tries to guide or reposition you, do you find yourself resisting them even when you don’t mean to?

I don’t really notice myself resisting people moving me, no. The problem is more that I’ll start doing things that don’t make sense, like lining receipts on the floor or tapping the calculator in patterns, and I don’t snap out of it right away.
Have there been times when you stopped speaking entirely, even when people were talking to you or expecting an answer?
No, I don’t think I’ve stopped speaking entirely like that. I might get quiet or take a bit to answer, but I don’t remember just not talking at all when someone was asking me something.
Do you ever repeat another person’s words exactly right after they say them?

No, I don’t think I repeat people’s words back right after they say them. It’s more that I end up doing odd things, like lining receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in sets of nine without really meaning to.
Have there been times when you became very physically restless or active in a way that seemed purposeless, like pacing or moving around a lot for no clear reason?

Yeah, kind of. I wouldn’t say it’s always just pacing, but I get really active with starting things. Like I’ll suddenly try to make templates for every client, email people about starting a study group, and then start planning out a bookkeeping service for small art studios, all before I’ve even finished the work that’s already due. It feels like I’m doing a lot, but it’s not really focused.
During these periods, do you become so physically agitated that you can’t seem to settle down, even when there’s nothing specific you’re trying to do?

Not really like I’m just agitated with nothing to do. It’s more like I can’t stop starting things. I’ll be making templates for every client, then emailing classmates about a study group, then sketching out some bookkeeping service idea for small art studios, all before I’ve even finished the work that’s already due.
Have you been neglecting basic self-care, like bathing or changing clothes, more than usual lately?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. I’m still bathing and changing clothes like usual, as far as I can tell.
Do you ever copy another person’s movements right after they do them?
No, I don’t think I do that. I haven’t noticed myself copying someone’s movements right after they do them.
